purpose: Albendazole is used to treat infections caused by certain parasitic worms, such as tapeworms and roundworms. It can treat worm infections in your intestines as well as in other parts of your body like your liver, lungs, or brain. Your doctor may prescribe it for conditions like neurocysticercosis or hydatid disease.
how_it_works: Albendazole works by blocking the worm's ability to absorb sugar (glucose), which is its main source of energy. Without energy, the worm becomes paralyzed and eventually dies. Your body then naturally eliminates the dead parasites over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, headache, and dizziness. Some people may notice a temporary rise in liver enzymes, which your doctor will monitor with blood tests. You may also experience a mild fever or temporary hair loss during treatment.
warnings: Do not take albendazole if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control during treatment and for one month after. Your doctor will check your liver function and blood counts with regular blood tests during treatment. Avoid this medication if you are allergic to albendazole or similar medications. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with albendazole.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on the type of infection being treated. A common adult dose is 400 mg taken twice a day with a fatty meal (like peanut butter or milk) to help your body absorb it better. Treatment can last anywhere from a few days to several months depending on your condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
